jobs.description:
Every day, tens of millions of people come to Roblox to explore, create, play, learn, and connect with friends in 3D immersive digital experiences– all created by our global community of developers and creators.

At Roblox, we’re building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience that they can imagine to life. Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world, and on any device. We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there.

A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.

As a User Researcher on the Platform & Foundation Design team, reporting directly to the Director of Design Strategy & Operations, you will generate actionable qualitative and quantitative insights that shape the platform and tools that empower our players, creators, and builders to bring their craft and vision to life. Embedded directly on product teams, you will conduct generative and evaluative research centered on how players engage, how creators build and grow, and how builders bring their ideas to life across the platform. You will tackle high-priority features, solve complex problems, and help translate foundational platform systems into intuitive, trustworthy, and scalable experiences. Partnering closely with Product, Product Design, Engineering, and Data Science, you will ensure user needs directly inform platform decisions while driving mutual value across players, creators, and builders.

You Will

Execute end-to-end mixed-methods research projects to understand how players, creators, and builders use Foundation UI and tools, translating abstract user behaviors into clear product feature recommendations.
Conduct foundational research to uncover key user pain points, mental models, and behaviors across creators, players, and builders to guide long-term UX strategy.
Work with cross-functional stakeholders in Design, Product, Policy, Legal, Engineering, and Data Science to facilitate research discussions and give concise feedback to inform feature roadmaps and product vision.
Partner with Analytics and Data Science to combine qualitative insights with behavioral platform data, building a holistic view of user engagement across the platform.
Work in close collaboration with cross-functional teams to evolve research processes and foster a culture of inclusion, collaboration, and innovation.
Have opportunities to present your research findings and strategic implications clearly to Product Group leadership.

You Have

5+ years of professional career experience as a UX or product researcher.
A Bachelor's, Master's or PhD in HCI, psychology, marketing research, sociology, anthropology, or other social science field with an emphasis on research, or equivalent work experience.
Knowledge about a variety of research methods. Is comfortable with both qualitative and quantitative methodology and can identify the correct methodology for the question at hand. Preferably has experience using software vendors like Qualtrics, database analysis with SQL and can conduct statistical analyses in SPSS, R or Python.
Engaged in collaboration and sharing work frequently, inviting feedback from peers and manager or supervisor
Solutions and a tuned thought process that ensure research will adequately answer questions and even challenge if the questions being asked are the right ones.
The ability to articulate and research findings clearly through verbal, written, and visual communication.

Role and Responsibilities

This Post Doctoral Research Scientist role sits within the core Machine Learning research team at Hewlett Packard Labs, HPE’s primary research organization, based in the San Francisco Bay Area. The team is recognized for award-winning, top-tier publications and foundational contributions spanning reinforcement learning for complex systems, fusion, large language models (LLMs), agentic AI, generative diffusion models, trustworthy AI, optimization, and digital twins.

Experience and deep knowledge of different deep learning model architectures, uncertainty quantification, optimization, control, digital twins, and world models.

NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. Today, we're tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. NVIDIA IT builds the products NVIDIANs use to get work done every day: the company intranet and mobile app, IT help and self-service, an AI personal assistant, and secure workspaces where employees run their own AI agents. We're hiring our first user experience researcher to answer a question that matters more every quarter: what makes people productive at NVIDIA, and what should we build, buy, or change so more people can work that way?

This is a senior, independent role with a long horizon. Our users are our colleagues, so access is never the bottleneck. You start with rich data: an annual IT survey with thousands of written comments from employees in 36 countries, support tickets, and product analytics. You'll set the research agenda, run the studies that matter most, and raise the research bar for the product managers and designers you work with.

What You'll Be Doing

Own a multi-quarter research program on how NVIDIANs work: what separates people who have adopted new ways of working, including AI tools, from those who haven't, and which tools, built or bought, would help the rest.
Shape our core products. Find the fundamental changes that would make our intranet, IT help, and AI assistant more useful, starting from questions like "what does a typical work day at NVIDIA look like?"
Pair field research (contextual inquiry, interviews, diary studies) with survey, support, and analytics data. Use AI to scale analysis without trading away validity.
Bring rigor. Choose methods that hold up (reliability, validity, sampling), and help the team distinguish between decisions that benefit from research vs. decisions that can just be made.
Raise the team's research craft. Coach PMs and designers on study design, interview guides, and live interviewing, and partner with designers on usability work
Build the practice from zero: a participant panel, consent and confidentiality standards for research with colleagues (with HR and Legal), and an insights repository so research compounds instead of repeating.
Turn findings into decisions. Present clear recommendations to IT leadership, define experience and adoption metrics with PMs, and follow through until insights shape roadmaps, not just fixes.

What We Need To See

12+ years in UX research or a closely related field, including leading strategic, multi-quarter research programs.
Master's or PhD in Human-Computer Interaction, Psychology, Cognitive Science, Anthropology, Sociology, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
Deep mixed-methods expertise: generative field research, survey design and analysis (including open text), and analysis of behavioral data.
A portfolio or case studies showing research that changed strategy, roadmap, or investment decisions, not only feature details.
Experience researching enterprise, internal, or workplace products used by employees.
Proven ability to work as the first or only researcher on a team: set the agenda, say no to low-value studies, and coach others on research craft.
Clear writing and presentation that moves senior leaders to a decision.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Research on AI tool adoption, knowledge-worker productivity, or how teams change the way they work.
Internal IT, employee experience, or workplace technology research.
Quantitative depth: SQL, R, or Python, and quasi-experimental designs (such as matched comparisons) that separate what drives adoption from what only correlates with it.
You've used LLMs to scale research synthesis and know where they fail.

🚀 About WRITER

WRITER is the AI platform built for the world’s most ambitious marketing and revenue teams, bringing the frontier of AI to the people who drive enterprise growth. With WRITER, autonomous agents work across the buyer journey, continuously executing on market signals and enterprise intelligence to grow revenue faster. Every agent action and asset is grounded in trust, built on an Enterprise Brain that unites brand, product, and company knowledge with fiduciary-grade governance and compliance.

Fortune 500 companies are transforming how they go to market with WRITER, including 3 of the top 5 US banks, 2 of the 5 largest global CPG conglomerates, and 4 of the top 5 US healthcare insurers. Founded in 2020, WRITER is backed by investors including Insight Partners, ICONIQ, Radical Ventures, Premji Invest, Balderton, B Capital, Salesforce Ventures, Adobe Ventures, Accenture, Citi Ventures, IBM Ventures, WndrCo, and others. Learn more at WRITER.com.

📐 About The Role

AI research at WRITER isn't just about publishing papers — it's about building the scientific foundation that powers some of the most ambitious enterprise AI deployments in the world. As an AI research scientist, you'll be at the center of that work. You'll drive a high-impact research agenda focused on large language models, agentic reasoning, and the system-level capabilities that make AI genuinely useful at enterprise scale. This is a rare opportunity to do research that matters twice over — advancing the field and shipping directly into products used by hundreds of thousands of people every day.

We're at an inflection point. Enterprises are moving from experimenting with AI to deeply embedding it across their operations, and WRITER's models are the engine making that possible. The work you do here — on post-training, planning, multi-step reasoning, and agentic workflows — will directly shape how the next generation of enterprise AI behaves, performs, and scales. You'll have the resources, infrastructure, and cross-functional support to pursue ambitious ideas and bring them to life quickly. This role is hybrid, based out of our San Francisco or New York City hub.

You'll report to our VP of AI research. Please note: role is open to Senior, Staff, and Sr. Staff applicants

We are open to hiring for this role at multiple levels, with compensation ranges scaled to match your experience, expertise, and the scope of the role.

🦸🏻‍♀️ What You'll Do

Lead an independent, high-impact research agenda on large language models and agentic systems, owning projects from early hypothesis through model training, evaluation, and production deployment
Design and execute large-scale post-training experiments using supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), RLAIF, DPO, and emerging alignment techniques — with a focus on improving multi-step reasoning, planning, and tool use in enterprise agentic workflows
Build novel evaluation benchmarks and methodologies that push beyond existing limitations, establishing rigorous measures for how well models perform on complex, real-world enterprise tasks

Shape WRITER's model architecture and training roadmap by translating your research insights into concrete improvements to our enterprise-grade LLMs, working hand-in-hand with research engineering and product teams
Publish and present original research at top-tier venues — NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, ACL, and others — representing WRITER at the frontier of the field and contributing to the broader scientific community

A Ph.D. in Computer Science, Machine Learning, NLP, or a related field — or equivalent demonstrated research experience with a strong portfolio of independent, published work
Expert-level knowledge of post-training methods including SFT, RLHF, RLAIF, DPO, GRPO, and related alignment and reasoning techniques, with a track record of applying them to real, production-grade systems
Strong command of Python and PyTorch (or JAX), with the engineering depth to build and scale training pipelines, evaluation infrastructure, and data synthesis workflows yourself — not just direct others to do it

Hands-on experience designing or evaluating agentic systems — models that plan, reason through multi-step tasks, use tools, and recover gracefully from errors — with a nuanced understanding of where they break and how to fix them

Humorphism concerns the quality of the working relationship between a person and an AI system. It asks whether the system acts proactively adapts to the person and the situation earns trust manages attention and strengthens human judgment. This role turns those behaviors into testable questions then answers them with working systems.

You will own the scientific agenda. You will convert a fuzzy behavioral goal into an end-to-end plan that covers data agent architecture evaluation and the product experiment that tests it. You will write code every week and build large parts of the experimental stack yourself because it does not exist yet.

The first focus areas are agentic products where a domain expert holds judgment the system cannot replace. Amazon Connect places an assistant beside a person handling a live conversation. AWS Bio Discovery places one beside a scientist running experiments. Both need evaluation that measures collaboration quality rather than task completion alone.

The role changes shape as the Lab matures. It starts as hands-on science in close partnership with product and engineering. Later it moves inside a product team to carry adoption of what the Lab proved.

Own the scientific strategy for human-AI collaboration across agentic and multimodal systems.
Convert desired interaction behaviors into falsifiable hypotheses evaluation tasks and system requirements.

Most days you build. You take a claim about how a teammate should behave design the smallest experiment that can falsify it and run it. You read interaction traces from real sessions then argue with the engineers about what they mean.

At a Glance

This is one of the highest-leverage quantitative research roles in the marketplace space right now. Here’s what you need to know before reading further.

Greenfield scope — you’ll co-create the quantitative research roadmap, not inherit one.
Pricing research at marketplace scale, a rare and technically rich problem space spanning guest behavior, host decision-making, and competitive dynamics.
Strategic seat at the table, Turo’s CEO is a strong advocate for research, and researchers are regularly invited into cross-functional leadership groups.
A close-knit team with a strong reputation as a high-performing, collaborative team across the organization.

Research at Turo isn’t a support function, it’s a strategic one. Embedded within the product and design organization, research is playing a core role in identifying and de-risking the opportunities that will define our next chapter, from pricing and marketplace dynamics to new revenue growth opportunities.

The team has earned a strong external reputation, with members speaking at The Learners Research Week, Sprig, and EPIC, and our guest segmentation work recently was nominated as a finalist for the 2026 ESOMAR Outstanding Contribution Award.

Turo is reinventing rental to unlock independence for all, with hundreds of thousands of vehicles listed by a vast network of local hosts across the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, France, and Australia. You'll work across some of our most strategically important domains, where you'll be our first researcher with a focus on pricing and marketplace dynamics. Pricing is one of the most powerful levers we have for driving guest demand and conversion, and it’s one of the most complex: because Turo is a peer-to-peer marketplace, hosts set their own prices, which means the research spans guest value perception, host pricing behavior, competitive positioning, and booking funnel merchandising. Lead quantitative research across pricing and marketplace domains, including guest willingness-to-pay, price elasticity, value perception, and host pricing behavior and decision-making.
Partner with product management, design, data, marketing, and strategy on research that informs product roadmaps, product development, and growth strategies.

Translate complex quantitative findings into compelling narratives that drive alignment across product, design, business, and leadership audiences.
Leverage AI-assisted tools to accelerate research velocity and help establish team standards for when and how to trust AI-generated outputs.
Mentor other researchers on quantitative methods, experimental design, and statistical rigor, and contribute to team playbooks and infrastructure.
Flex into qualitative methods (i.e. interviews, usability studies, or mixed-methods triangulation, etc.) when the question calls for it.

8+ years of professional research experience, with at least 4 years of quantitative UX research on consumer software across multiple surfaces (Desktop, Mobile Web, iOS, Android).
A strong portfolio of quantitative studies that demonstrably shaped product strategy and roadmap decisions — not just informed them.
Deep expertise in experimental design, survey methodology, statistical analysis, and behavioral data analysis.
Proficiency in R, Python, and/or SQL; experience analyzing large datasets and surfacing actionable patterns.
Experience with pricing research methods (conjoint, van Westendorp, willingness-to-pay, elasticity modeling) a core skill for this role, not a bonus.
Experience conducting research on a two-sided marketplace, platform, or peer-to-peer product.
Experience partnering with Data Engineering or Analytics teams on instrumentation, logging, or pipeline work.
Demonstrated fluency with AI-assisted research tools and a considered point of view on their appropriate use.
Exceptional storytelling skills, able to translate quantitative complexity into narratives that land with PMs, data scientists, and executive audiences alike.
Strong stakeholder management, including the ability to push back with confidence and redirect scope when priorities demand it.
A primary identity as a quantitative researcher, with comfort flexing into qualitative methods when the question calls for it.
Bachelor’s degree required in a relevant field.

Masters or PhD in Human-Computer Interaction, Psychology, Data Science, Statistics, Behavioral Economics, or a related field.
Experience in transportation, travel, mobility, or marketplace/growth-focused product teams.
Familiarity with causal inference methods (diff-in-diff, regression discontinuity, propensity score matching).

This is one of the highest-leverage quantitative research roles in the marketplace space right now. Here’s what you need to know before reading further.

Research at Turo isn’t a support function, it’s a strategic one. You'll work across some of our most strategically important domains, where you'll be our first researcher with a focus on pricing and marketplace dynamics. Leverage AI-assisted tools to accelerate research velocity and help establish team standards for when and how to trust AI-generated outputs.

8+ years of professional research experience, with at least 4 years of quantitative UX research on consumer software across multiple surfaces (Desktop, Mobile Web, iOS, Android).
A strong portfolio of quantitative studies that demonstrably shaped product strategy and roadmap decisions — not just informed them.
Deep expertise in experimental design, survey methodology, statistical analysis, and behavioral data analysis.

Experience conducting research on a two-sided marketplace, platform, or peer-to-peer product.
Experience partnering with Data Engineering or Analytics teams on instrumentation, logging, or pipeline work.
Demonstrated fluency with AI-assisted research tools and a considered point of view on their appropriate use.
Exceptional storytelling skills, able to translate quantitative complexity into narratives that land with PMs, data scientists, and executive audiences alike.

A primary identity as a quantitative researcher, with comfort flexing into qualitative methods when the question calls for it.

Experience in transportation, travel, mobility, or marketplace/growth-focused product teams.
